Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the run chase. The umpires walk to the middle followed by the Australian women's side who settle to their respective field positions. Smriti Mandhana and Yastika Bhatia are the two openers for India Women. While Megan Schutt will open the bowling for Australia Women.
... RUN CHASE ...

The Indian bowlers were put under pressure by the Australian batters but they did well in the middle phase and pulled things back a bit. Shreyanka Patil was the pick of the bowlers as she picked up 3 wickets while Amanjot Kaur picked up a couple. Pooja Vastrakar and Deepti Sharma took a wicket each as well. The pitch looks dry and it will assist the spinners a bit but if dew comes the batters would enjoy it as it would get difficult for the bowlers to grip the ball. An exciting run chase to follow in a while.

The centurion, Phoebe Litchfield is in for a chat. She says that it was a very good wicket to bat on and she was patient on the pitch. She also states that there were a lot of scoring opportunities as four fielders were outside the inner circle. Also says that she was a bit nervous in her nineties but the end went well. She thought they could push a bit more but a few wickets in the middle pushed them back. She feels that they finished well and she also praises the way Alana King and Georgia Wareham played at the end.

Skipper Alyssa Healy would be delighted with the way her side has responded after she asked them to bat first as they scored 338 runs in their quota of 50 overs. After opting to bat first, the Aussies started a bit watchfully but with some positive intent as they scored 55 without losing any wicket off the Powerplay and did not let go of any loose delivery. The opening stand was brilliant between Alyssa Healy and Phoebe Litchfield as they managed to score 189 together. Phoebe Litchfield held her ground well and scored a well-crafted century as she went on to score 119 runs while Alyssa Healy did well with the bat too as she scored 82. Ellyse Perry walked in at number but could not do much and it was the same case with Beth Mooney and Tahlia McGrath but Ashleigh Gardner and Annabel Sutherland played key knocks. As she did in the last game, Alana King played a quickfire cameo so did Georgia Wareham to take Australia Women to 338.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the third ODI to commence. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the middle. It will be Phoebe Litchfield and Alyssa Healy to open the innings for Australia Women. Renuka Singh will start with the new ball for India Women. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Murali Kartik is pitchside. He starts by informing that pitch number 8 will be used for this game. Mentions that the straight boundaries are longer than the square ones. States that there is a presence of grass on this wicket but it is very dry and barren underneath. Mentions that we saw an appreciable turn in the last game and he expects more of the same in this game as well. Reckons that spinners will be a handful in this game as well.

The captain of India Women, Harmanpreet Kaur says that they were looking to bowl first. Informs that Sneh Rana misses out and Mannat Kashyap will make her debut. She feels the last game was really close but they will put more awareness and take more responsibility. She states they could have won the last game but it was a good learning for them.

Alyssa Healy, the skipper of Australia Women, says that they will bat first. On a lighter note, she says that she will never change on calling tails. Says this looks like a good batting track in the day and feels that it will break a bit later and assist the bowlers. Mentions that they have one change with Megan Schutt coming in for Darcie Brown. Adds that they can not underestimate this Indian team and with the World Cup on the horizon, they would be looking to play a positive brand of cricket and also try out some combinations.

Australia Women (Playing XI) - Alyssa Healy (C/WK), Phoebe Litchfield, Ellyse Perry, Beth Mooney, Tahlia McGrath, Ashleigh Gardner, Annabel Sutherland, Georgia Wareham, Alana King, Kim Garth, Megan Schutt (In for Darcie Brown).

India Women (Playing XI) - Yastika Bhatia, Smriti Mandhana, Richa Ghosh (WK), Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Jemimah Rodrigues, Deepti Sharma, Amanjot Kaur, Pooja Vastrakar, Renuka Singh, Shreyanka Patil, Mannat Kashyap (On ODI debut)(In for Sneh Rana).
TOSS - Australia Women have won the coin toss and they will BAT first.

On the other side, India Women have only themselves to blame, as they were sloppy in the field and could not handle the pressure at the back end of their run chase. Due to their disappointing performance in fielding, they gave away extra lives to the opposition batters, which came back to haunt them. With the ball, Deepti Sharma stood out with a five-wicket haul. In reply, India Women got off to a steady start and had the game under control, all thanks to Richa Ghosh. India lost their way after her dismissal and fell 3 runs short to concede the series defeat. Can the Women in Blue end the series with a win? Let's find out. Toss and teams coming up shortly...

In the last outing, Australia Women showed why they are the world champions as they managed to steal a victory from India's grasp by defending their score well. While batting first, both Phoebe Litchfield and Ellyse Perry got excellent fifties to set up a good platform. After Perry's dismissal, they lost wickets at regular intervals but ended with a fighting total thanks to Georgia Wareham and Alana King's late contributions. The bowling unit had a lot of work to do as they didn't have too many runs to defend. The game went down to the wire but Ashleigh Gardner and Annabel Sutherland kept their nerves at the death to seal the win for their side. Alyssa Healy and her side will look to dish out a whitewash and by doing so, extend their dominance over India Women.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of the 3rd ODI between India Women and Australia Women at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai. Australia hold an unassailable 2-0 lead in the series, whereas India will look to avoid the clean sweep and end the series on a high.
... MATCH DAY ...

Mumbai's iconic Wankhede Stadium will be the setting again as India Women and Australia Women lock horns in the third and final ODI of the series. After the Aussies registered a comfortable victory in the series opener, it was a tightly contested second ODI that went down the wire, but it were the visitors again who came out on top. As a result, Australia Women have taken an unassailable lead in the series, whereas India Women have more than just pride to play for in the final game. With the T20I series to follow, the Women in Blue will look to end the ODI series with a win and gain some much-needed momentum. After Alyssa Healy called it right and opted to bat first in the second ODI, Phoebe Litchfield's 63 and Ellyse Perry's 50, along with lower-order contributions, took Australia to a competitive total. In reply, India started well and had the game under control for most parts. However, Richa Ghosh fell 4 runs short of her maiden ODI ton and after that, none of the incoming batters were able to take the hosts over the line. Moreover, Harmanpreet Kaur and her side dropped as many as 7 catches which eventually came back to haunt them. As they look to avoid the clean sweep, they will have to pull up their socks and support the bowlers in the field. Other than Ghosh, Smriti Mandhana and Jemimah Rodrigues got starts but failed to make it count, and that is one aspect they would want to improve on. It was a hard-fought victory for Australia, and it would have tasted sweeter than their win in the first game. The tourists hung in there and held their nerves towards the end to seal the deal. Having sealed the series, Australia would want to dish out a whitewash and start the year right. Like India, Australia were tardy in the field, something which we do not associate with the Aussies, and Alyssa Healy will be hoping for improvement in the field. Considering that Phoebe Litchfield and Ellyse Perry have done the bulk of the scoring, the rest of the batting unit will want to get some runs under their belt ahead of the T20I series. Will Australia manage to inflict a whitewash? Or will India pull one back and avoid the clean sweep? We shall find out together.
